periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water is 11%, green against the <=12% target, and this is our starting point for the eight-quarter run. The September water balance tied out cleanly after Meter Services re-read the 400 large accounts on Route L-17 and corrected two stuck compound meters at Harborview Medical and Pier Cold Storage. Field crews also closed 31 leak tickets in DMAs 2, 4, and 6, with the worst service-line loss on asset SL-04418 repaired before it became a main-side problem. The pipes are not getting younger, but this quarter says the system is still behaving like an AA-rated utility should.
periods.recommendations: Hold the monthly district-metered-area review and keep the Route L-17 large-meter verification in the standard work, not as a one-off cleanup. Extend acoustic listening on the downtown loop from hydrants H-221 through H-246 before winter pressure changes start moving small leaks around. Keep tagging every confirmed loss to an asset ID so the next budget ask is backed by pipe, not adjectives.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water moved from 11% to 11.1%, up 0.1 percentage points quarter over quarter, still green against the <=12% target. That is a small drift, and it matches what we saw in December when night-flow in DMA 4 rose after the first cold snap and then settled after Crew B repaired the 6-inch cast-iron joint near Oak Street, asset WM-1937. Billing-to-production timing was also a little rough because the holiday read cycle pushed 1,842 residential meters into the following week. I am not calling 0.1 percentage points a trend by itself, but I am writing it down because water loss likes to start quietly.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the weekly night-flow pull for DMAs 3, 4, and 6 and add a simple exception flag when minimum flow rises more than 8% for two nights. Keep Meter Services on the holiday-cycle reconciliation so apparent losses do not hide real ones. For the green result, extend winter leak listening to the older cast-iron grid west of Seabright before the January freeze-thaw window.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water is 11.2%, up 0.1 percentage points from 11.1%, and remains green. The increase is modest, but it is the second small step up, so we treated it as an engineering question instead of a dashboard footnote. Crew A found three curb-stop leaks during the March acoustic sweep on Routes N-08 and N-09, and the AMI vendor flagged 214 meters with flatline reads that were corrected before closeout. Production meter PM-02 at the North Plant also passed calibration at 0.4% variance, so I am less worried about source metering and more focused on distribution-side seepage.
periods.recommendations: Continue the acoustic sweep schedule and move the next pass to the higher-pressure hill zone around Reservoir 3, where small leaks become expensive faster. Maintain quarterly calibration on PM-02 and add PM-05 to the same work order bundle so source data stays boring. Use the flatline-meter cohort from Q1 as the target list for a 60-day replacement push, starting with accounts over 1.5 million gallons per year.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water reached 11.3%, up 0.1 percentage points from 11.2%, still green and still under the <=12% target. This is now a controlled creep rather than noise: three consecutive quarters of +0.1 percentage points. The June irrigation ramp added legitimate demand, but the South Beach pressure district showed higher overnight flow even after we removed seasonal usage from the calculation. Crew C repaired a leaking 8-inch valve bonnet on asset V-778 near Mariner Way, which should help Q3, but the pressure loggers tell me the older asbestos-cement laterals are contributing more than one valve.
periods.recommendations: Keep the green result green by extending pressure logging in South Beach for another 45 days, with loggers on PRV-12, PRV-14, and hydrant H-510. Fold the valve-bonnet repair data into the asset condition register and rank adjacent valves for inspection before paving season locks us out. Bring a short Q2 water-loss brief to the capital review so the laterals are visible before they become an emergency line item.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water is 11.5%, up 0.2 percentage points from 11.3%, and remains green, but the slope got steeper. Summer demand always exposes weak pipe, and this quarter the weak spots were not theoretical: crews handled recurring service leaks on Bayshore Route B-12 and a pinhole cluster on the 1958 ductile segment WM-2284. The main system stayed in service, which matters, but unbilled loss is now closing distance to the 12% ceiling. This is exactly where we defend renewal dollars with evidence, because the pipes are voting in gallons.
periods.recommendations: Sustain the DMA night-flow program and extend it to Bayshore Route B-12 with two weeks of overnight correlation before the fall rains mask the signal. Advance design scoping for WM-2284 under the Pipeline Renewal candidate list, including potholing at the two utility conflicts by Harbor Lane. Keep the AMI exception reports going weekly and separate apparent loss from real loss in the next scorecard note.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water rose from 11.5% to 11.7%, up 0.2 percentage points, still green but no longer comfortable. The Q4 water audit points to a mix of real loss and meter aging: 27 small leaks were repaired, but 18 of them were on the same pre-1970 neighborhoods we already have circled in red pencil on the wall map. The large-meter test bench found two under-registering turbine meters at the marina accounts, which explains part of the loss, not all of it. We are below 12%, but the quarter-over-quarter pattern is now six quarters of upward movement from the 11% baseline.
periods.recommendations: Replace the two marina turbine meters before the February read cycle and verify the correction in the billing-to-production reconciliation. Keep Pipeline Renewal design work moving for the pre-1970 Bayshore and South Beach segments, with WM-2284 and WM-1937 in the first cut. For the green status, sustain the current leak-response staffing through winter instead of relaxing it just because the indicator has not crossed the line.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water is 11.9%, up 0.2 percentage points from 11.7%, still green by one tenth against the <=12% target. That is a thin margin, and I do not like thin margins on buried infrastructure. January freeze-thaw produced seven main-side leaks, including the repeat repair on WM-1937 at Oak Street, and the temporary bypass meters showed measurable loss before the clamp work was complete. The crews kept outages short and the books still show green, but the asset condition story is getting louder.
periods.recommendations: Hold the line by assigning Crew B and the leak-detection contractor to WM-1937, WM-2284, and the South Beach laterals before spring paving starts. Move the top Pipeline Renewal packages from concept to 30% design, with cost estimates that separate leak reduction from service reliability benefits. Keep the scorecard green work active: monthly production-meter calibration, weekly AMI exceptions, and DMA night-flow review should remain mandatory until we see at least two flat quarters.

periods.analysis: Non-Revenue Water is 12.8%, up 0.9 percentage points from 11.9%, and has moved to yellow above the <=12% target but below the >14% red threshold. This is the first quarter where the long creep turned into a real operating concern, and the jump lines up with the May main break on WM-2284 plus elevated night-flow in South Beach DMA 6 after the repair. We recovered service and isolated the leak field, but the temporary clamps and bypass work left enough loss in the quarter to show up plainly in the water balance. The problem is serious, actively managed, and now directly tied to the Pipeline Renewal work rather than treated as routine leak chasing.
periods.recommendations: Put WM-2284 and the adjacent South Beach laterals into the first Pipeline Renewal construction release, and authorize the procurement package for pipe, valves, and traffic control before the vendor lead times get longer. For the yellow watch item, require a weekly DMA 6 night-flow report and a 30-day post-repair water balance to confirm the 12.8% does not become the new floor. Keep Crew C on targeted leak correlation in Bayshore and South Beach, and bring Council a short evidence packet showing the quarter-over-quarter +0.9 percentage point movement, repair history, and expected loss reduction.

periods.analysis: Illustrative September import: non-revenue water rose from 12.8% to 13.4%, exceeding the 12% target. The earlier South Beach DMA 6 night-flow concern remains a lead to investigate, not proof of the cause of this quarter’s increase.
periods.recommendations: Reconcile the DMA 6 night-flow reports and post-repair water balance with the system-wide calculation. Prioritize confirmed leaks and meter discrepancies before forecasting savings from renewal.
